speaker: Ramon Vega
cascadeSummary: I am tabling review of the Ivy Hill Community Support Initiative until the Clerk verifies the filing or the record establishes that it did not occur; a prior claim is not a filing reference. For Glenview, the supplied record does not establish what the civic response meeting found or what work was done, so I am requesting a documented account, a responsible department, and a next update date. I remain prepared to support the Grand Lake proposal with its safeguards intact, without claiming a recorded outcome before the roll exists.

statements.topic: Ivy Hill Community Support Initiative filing verification
statements.decision: Table council review until the Clerk provides a filing reference or the record explicitly establishes that filing has not occurred.
statements.quote: A filing claim is not a Clerk reference; verify the record before we take it up.
statements.fullStatement: I said last cycle that the Ivy Hill legislation had been filed, but the current record gives me no Clerk reference to verify that claim. I will not proceed to council review on an unverified filing. The Clerk should provide the reference, or establish plainly that filing has not occurred; until then, this item is tabled. That is a process correction, not a judgment that Ivy Hill needs an emergency label. The evidence in this packet describes soured mood, slow trade, and low crime, and the review should proceed on a verified record.

statements.decision: Request neighborhood-specific attention proportionate to the reported conditions, with documented follow-through on Glenview's public-works spike.
statements.quote: Take the Glenview spike seriously, document the work, and do not turn it into a citywide crisis.
statements.fullStatement: In District 4, Glenview has a medium-severity public-works spike even as its mood is mildly positive; its street trade is slow and crime is low. Ivy Hill's mood has soured, with slow trade and low crime. Dimond is flat, with slow trade, low crime, and a zoning adjustment; its mood has held steady. These are different neighborhood conditions, not one emergency. I want staff follow-through tied to the actual issue in each place, and a clear account of the Glenview work, without claiming more than the record supports.

statements.decision: Request that staff document the meeting's findings and any work performed, reconcile the reported severity, name the responsible department, and provide the next public update date.
statements.quote: The meeting is not a finding; tell residents what was learned, what was done, and who reports next.
statements.fullStatement: The Cycle 115 city summary records a Glenview Civic Response Meeting and describes a low-severity public-works spike. This cycle's brief reports a medium-severity spike, but supplies no meeting findings, work record, responsible department, or next update date. I cannot responsibly say what staff found or what work was performed. Please publish those details, reconcile the severity descriptions, identify the department responsible for any remaining work, and give residents a next public update date. Until that account is in the record, I cannot conclude that follow-through is complete or that no further municipal action is needed.

statements.decision: Maintain a YES position with the milestone and audit conditions intact; do not claim an outcome before the recorded roll.
statements.quote: I remain for the proposal with its safeguards intact; the roll, not this statement, records the decision.
statements.fullStatement: My position on Commercial Stabilization for Grand Lake remains YES, with the milestone and audit conditions intact. That support does not substitute for the recorded full-council vote, and I will not describe an outcome before the roll exists. The conditions are part of the case for the proposal, not details to be dropped after a hearing. I ask that the Clerk record the council's decision clearly so residents can distinguish a member's stated position from the final result.
